newsitem.title: GERMANY: EMU a unique chance for Euro markets - Vereinsbank.
newsitem.headline: EMU a unique chance for Euro markets - Vereinsbank.

text.p: Europe's planned single currency will give its fractured capital markets a unique opportunity to compete head to head with those in the U.S., Germany's Bayerische Vereinsbank AG said on Friday.

In a research paper, the bank said the euro should boost liquidity on bond and share markets, support innovation through rising competition and improve market structures as individual markets gear up to face global competitors.

"The euro can catapult European capital markets from the second to the first division...(It) has the chance to become the second largest international investment currency after the dollar," Vereinsbank said.
The bank welcomed the planned development of a euro-denominated bond market, which it said could be worth some $4.5 trillion, second only to the U.S.

The figure assumes EMU will take place with eight starting members -- Germany, France, Belgium, Netherlands, Luxembourg, Austria, Ireland and Finland. Italy was unlikely to be in the starting group, Vereinsbank said.

The impact on equities will be less dramatic but the switch to the euro should also significantly improve European share liquidity by breaking down barriers to cross-border equity investment, Vereinsbank said.
Given the participation of the above countries, the EMU zone equity market would be the third largest in the world after the U.S. and Japan.

In the longer term, European equity culture would benefit from a gradual trend toward privatisation, largely in response to government efforts to keep their budget deficits low as the Maasetricht Treaty requires, it added.
The bank estimated the market value of such EMU-driven privatisations at $300 billion.
